conventions.convention: Plane subharmonic functions take values in [-infinity,infinity), are upper semicontinuous, satisfy the circle submean inequality, and are not identically -infinity on a connected component.
A superharmonic function is exactly the negative of a subharmonic function, so it is lower semicontinuous and may take +infinity.
The Perron family is the lower family of subharmonic functions whose interior boundary limsup does not exceed the continuous datum.
The raw Perron envelope is the pointwise supremum U_phi, while the object called the regularized Perron envelope is H_phi=U_phi^*.
A barrier is global on the bounded domain, negative everywhere, tends to zero at the marked boundary point, and has a uniform negative boundary limsup away from every neighbourhood of that point.
Principal values use coupled symmetric truncations and do not imply separate improper convergence.
Residue contours are declared positively oriented; the keyhole branch has Arg z in (0,2 pi), and upper and lower indentation arcs have the directions explicitly given in the definition.
An admissible residue cycle has trace disjoint from the pole set and is null-homologous in the ambient open set.

The page uses a simultaneous-extension definition of domain of holomorphy: one fixed pair U1,U2 must work for every holomorphic function, while an individual extension is required to agree only on a nonempty open overlap.
H(r,s) uses z1 as the annular variable and z2 as the thin/full-disc variable; its hull is the full unit bidisc.

load_bearing.statement: A function u:Omega→[-infinity,infinity) is subharmonic when it is upper semicontinuous, is not identically -infinity on a connected component, and satisfies the circle submean inequality on every closed disc compactly contained in Omega.

Let Omega be open, let f be meromorphic on Omega with pole set S, and let Gamma be admissible for the residue theorem in Omega. Then the integral over Gamma equals 2 pi i times the finite sum of n(Gamma,a) Res(f,a) over a in S.

For u:Omega→[-infinity,infinity), subharmonicity is equivalent to upper semicontinuity, nontriviality on each component, and comparison with every continuous harmonic majorant on every compactly contained disc.
Fix 0<r,s<1. Every holomorphic function on the Hartogs figure H(r,s) admits a unique holomorphic extension to the bidisc hull.
For a bounded complex domain and continuous real boundary datum, the regularized Perron envelope is harmonic on the domain.
The Poisson modification is well defined, subharmonic on Omega, harmonic on the modified disc, and majorizes the original subharmonic function.
A boundary point of a bounded complex plane domain is regular if and only if the domain admits a barrier there.
A separately holomorphic function on a finite-dimensional polydisc is bounded on every smaller closed polydisc; in particular it is locally bounded.
If m≥2 and f is holomorphic on Omega minus one point a, then f extends uniquely to a holomorphic function on Omega.
Every holomorphic function on the specified coordinate shell S(a,rho;r,s) extends uniquely to the whole polydisc Delta_rho(a).
Under the stated local-extension and component-overlap hypotheses, every holomorphic function on G extends uniquely to G union U1 union ... union UN.

concerns.concern: The final remark says agreement on one overlap makes the definition independent of the overlap. The intersection of two connected domains can be disconnected, and branches such as logarithms can agree on one intersection component but differ on another, so the remark is false as written.

The declared positive keyhole orientation reverses both lips: for the slit annulus with Arg in (0,2 pi), the upper lip should run from epsilon to R and the lower lip from R to epsilon. The stated lower-semicircle parametrization is also negatively oriented despite the blanket positive-orientation convention.

This definition permits an arbitrary open Omega while its cited meromorphic-function definition is only for a nonempty connected plane domain. No componentwise convention is supplied, so 'f meromorphic on Omega in the sense of' the cited definition is ill-typed for disconnected Omega.

Part 1 allows zero coefficients although subharmonic functions may equal -infinity. Thus 0 times u is undefined at such a point unless a convention is supplied; the statement and proof both use that product.

Step 2.1 establishes integrability only on one disc centered at a finite-valued point inside the chosen smaller disc. Step 3.1 then claims arbitrary compact sets are covered by discs 'of the form constructed' without showing such a disc exists around every point. The polar-coordinate conversion of integrated circle averages to an area integral is also unstated.

Step 3.1 checks the centered circle behavior of log|z-a| but does not justify the submean inequality for arbitrary discs whose circles surround a. It also uses closure under positive sums before citing the later closure lemma.

Step 2.1 invokes harmonic comparison on the non-disc regions B intersect D and B minus the closure of D by saying shrinking discs suffice. The cited comparison theorem is only stated for discs, and the required maximum/comparison argument across the lens-shaped components is not supplied.

The exterior-disc function log(R/|z-c|) can vanish at other boundary contact points, so it need not be uniformly negative away from zeta. The sector power function is only local and may approach zero on sector sides. Neither construction is globalized before being called a barrier.
The proof applies a gluing lemma stated only across a disc boundary to an arbitrary neighbourhood W. The statement neither assumes W is a disc nor cites a general open-set gluing result.

Hypothesis 3 writes sup_K q for compact K contained in the closure of Omega intersect U, but q is defined only on the open set Omega intersect U. Boundary values of q are therefore not defined, and step 1.1 repeats the same evaluation on a closed seam.

Step 1.1 asserts that the complement G of the connected set E' is connected, which is false for a general planar continuum. The subsequent simple-connectivity and logarithm argument therefore does not follow as written, and the weak-peak separation condition is not checked.

The absence of a harmonic solution shows only that not all boundary points are regular. The conclusion 'in particular, the puncture is irregular' additionally needs the outer circle points to be shown regular, or a direct computation of the Perron envelope.

The pole set is closed and discrete only relative to Omega. Step 3.1 treats its intersection with the compact closure of U as a closed discrete subset without first proving that this closure lies inside Omega; that missing fact requires null-homology plus local constancy.

Step 3.1 says f is holomorphic on Omega minus A, but A contains only the poles of nonzero index. Poles of zero index remain. The homology comparison must instead be performed in Omega minus the entire pole set.

The statement allows an arbitrary isolated singularity, while the proof writes f as Res(f,a)/(z-a) plus a holomorphic function. For f(z)=1/(z-a)^2 on a nonclosed arc, the arc integral generally diverges as epsilon tends to zero although the residue is zero.

The formula incorrectly depends on an independently chosen upper/lower sign. In an upper-half-plane closure, a lower indentation encloses the real pole and adds its full residue. For R(z)=1/[z(z^2+1)] with a lower indentation, the principal value is 0 while the displayed formula gives -2 pi i.
The real-pole case inherits the false signed-indentation rule: a lower indentation in an upper contour changes which poles are enclosed, not merely the sign of the small-arc contribution.

With the lip orientations used in step 1.2, the contour contribution is (1-e^(2 pi i alpha)) times the real integral and equals +2 pi i times the residue sum, not the stated negative multiple. The statement also conflicts with the lip directions in the contour definition.

Using the theorem's stated negative-residue formula gives a positive 2 pi i e^(i pi alpha) numerator. Dividing by 1-e^(2 pi i alpha)=-2 i e^(i pi alpha) sin(pi alpha) gives -pi/sin(pi alpha), not the claimed positive value. The correct positive answer requires correcting the theorem's sign.
The statement uses C^(m-1) without fixing or quantifying m. The proof requires coordinates of z' and a several-variable separate-holomorphy theorem, so an explicit dimension hypothesis is required.

Step 1.1 says the punctured-slice lemma directly supplies a jointly holomorphic extension on the product. That lemma only proves holomorphic dependence of the missing value and slice-by-slice removability; a separate local-boundedness and joint-holomorphy argument is still needed.

Step 7.1 reverses an integral inequality. For nonpositive w_j and D(q,t/2) contained in D(z,t), the integral over the smaller disc is generally greater than, not less than, the integral over the larger disc. The claimed uniform coefficient bound and the rest of the proof do not follow.

Under the page's extension definition, an extension to U_j need agree with the old function only on some nonempty open part of U_j intersect G. The proof assumes agreement on every component of that intersection, so even the first gluing step and the asserted uniqueness are not licensed by the stated hypotheses.

Assumption 1 supplies an extension from one coordinate shell inside each P_j, but the proof promotes this to compatible agreement on all components of P_j intersect (Omega minus K). The component condition does not say every such component meets the shell, so the propagation lemma cannot be applied as claimed.

The witness 1/z1 is appropriate, but the proof does not quantify over the fixed U1,U2 pair in the domain-of-holomorphy definition. It should argue that if an extension F on connected U2 agreed on U1, then z1F=1 on U1 and hence on U2, contradicting any point of U2 with z1=0.

seams_checked.note: The citing page uses monotone convergence only for increasing nonnegative functions M-phi_n and M-u_n, matching thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral. Its separate-holomorphy lemma invokes Fatou only for the nonnegative measurable functions -w_j on Euclidean discs, matching thm-fatou-lemma. No domain, quantifier, hypothesis, direction, or conclusion is strengthened at the seam; the later geometric inequality in that proof is defective independently of the citation.
